sources.entry: easyocr - Ready-to-use OCR with 80+ languages supported.

summary.one_liner: EasyOCR is a Python library that reads text from images using pretrained models across 80+ languages and many writing scripts.
summary.what_it_does: The library detects and recognizes text in images through a `Reader` object that loads language models once and then runs on image file paths, OpenCV/numpy arrays, image bytes, or raw image URLs. Each result is a bounding box, the detected text, and a confidence score, or just the text when `detail=0` is set. Model weights for the chosen languages are downloaded automatically or can be placed manually in a local model folder. It can run on GPU or in CPU-only mode (`gpu=False`). A command-line entry point (`easyocr -l ... -f ...`) is also provided. The README says detection uses the CRAFT algorithm and recognition uses a CRNN model, and it describes training and custom-language guidelines, with a Dockerfile provided.
use_cases: extract text from photos or scanned images
read Chinese, Arabic, or Cyrillic text from pictures
pull text and coordinates from screenshots
run OCR on a server without a GPU
add OCR to a Gradio or web app
notable: Supports 80+ languages and many scripts, including Latin, Chinese, Arabic, Devanagari, and Cyrillic
Accepts file paths, numpy image arrays, image bytes, or image URLs
Command-line interface plus a Python API
Automatic model download, or manual placement in a model folder
Documented guidelines for contributing a new language via character and dictionary files
caveats: Not all languages can be combined in one Reader; the README says some languages are incompatible with each other
Handwritten text support is listed as upcoming, not currently available
The README says GPU use needs the correct CUDA build of torch, and Windows users must install torch and torchvision first
